items.title: ON Semiconductor Stock Is Already Half Off Its High, So How Low Could A Market Shock Take It?
items.summary: ON Semiconductor (ON) stock trades near $67, about 50% below its 52-week high. It lost 43.7% over the trailing three months, ending with a 9.0% fall on September 16. Yet it is still up 38.4% over the trailing twelve months, against 15.5% for the S&P 500. The company's latest results show a business still shrinking but recovering, not one in trouble.

items.title: MCHP's Analog AI Deal Gains Momentum: Can It Outpace NXPI & TXN?
items.summary: Microchip Technology expands its edge-AI push as AnalogAI adopts SST's memBrain SAGE IP for ultra-low-power processors in robots, drones and vehicles.

items.title: NXP Semiconductors NV's Dividend Analysis
items.summary: This article first appeared on GuruFocus.  NXP Semiconductors NV (NASDAQ:NXPI) recently announced a total dividend of $1.01 per share, with the ex-dividend date set for 2026-09-16.  This payment includes a $1.01 per share cash dividend payable on 2026-10-08.

items.title: Smartphone Chip Stocks Rally While Large-Cap Technology Slips: Skyworks Jumps 11%, Qorvo Rises 7%, Qualcomm Climbs 4%
items.summary: Three handset chip names are surging while the rest of large-cap tech slides lower, and no earnings release or analyst note explains the divergence. The reason behind the rotation tells you something important about where semiconductor money is quietly moving.

items.title: Should You Buy Cirrus Logic Stock Because Its Buyback Got Cheaper?
items.summary: Cirrus Logic (CRUS) stock has fallen about 27% in three months and trades roughly a third below its 52-week high. Investors are weighing a PC year that just got pushed out against a share count that keeps shrinking anyway. The buyback behind that is sturdier than the tape suggests: third in line for the cash, and still comfortably funded.

items.title: NXP Semiconductors Eyes Physical AI Leadership, Sees Data Center Growth Surge
items.summary: NXP Semiconductors (NASDAQ:NXPI) is positioning its portfolio around “physical AI,” with Chief Executive Officer Rafael Sotomayor saying the company aims to apply its longstanding strengths in security, functional safety, real-time processing and reliability to increasingly intelligent edge devices.
